row.notes: Session module slot 0x58 (vtable 0x1457f82e8 holds 0x142f45960; called through call [rax+0x58] at 0x14080c546 in Game_GameModule_OnSessionEnter's module loop). Walks the session's vehicle entities, a pointer vector module+0x28..+0x30 whose count is the byte ((end-begin)>>3)&0xff: copies the config at module+0x190..+0x268 into each entity's component 0x146ce8a00, and stores each entity's component 0x146ce8b00 into a 26-slot table at module+0xb0 with its count at module+0x180 and no bound check, so a 27th vehicle writes the count itself (crash at +0x2e9 writing, +0x305 reading, Send Logs 2026-10-29 sessions 111311/122524, rbp=r14=0x1b). Later loops reuse the vector count (vehicle controllers via 0x146096578, flags +0x132, +0x2580, +0x9f2c..). Reads the mode context at module+0x80: *(*(+0x88)+0x260) is the EntrantsManager, whose +0x2b0 (current game setup mode) it reads. | E3 2026-11-18 (engine-re, static): the last loop copies the session settings S = [module+0x78]+0x1a8 into every car: CarLive+0x9f2c = S+0xe10 ^ S+0xe18 (PU wear scale, read by Car_Engine_UpdateWear and Car_Ers_StepWear_Body), +0x9f30 = S+0xe20 ^ S+0xe28 (gearbox wear scale, Car_GearBox_UpdateShiftTimersAndFaults), +0x9f34 = 1.0, +0x9f38 = S+0xe30 ^ S+0xe38, +0x9f3c = S+0xe40 ^ S+0xe48 (store 0x142f460fc..0x142f46124). Runs at session enter only, so an addon that writes CarLive+0x9f2c / +0x9f30 after that keeps its value for the session (the only other static writer is the car create 0x144628190, which sets +0x9f2c..+0x9f38 to 1.0 at 0x144628df3; .xtls/.xtext/.data1 disp scan).

Table: lea [rsi+0xb0], store at 0x142f45a09 mov [rsi+rcx*8+0xb0] with rcx=[rsi+0x180], no compare against 26, so slot 26 is +0x180 (the count); the second loop 0x142f45c5a..0x142f45cc0 reads table entries up to the count (crash sites 0x142f45c49/0x142f45c65). Clamp check (guard (b) in era_picker.cpp sets [rsi+0x30]=begin+26*8 around the call): memory-safe here, the table gets 26 entries and count 26; the other table readers in the vtable, slot 0x20 0x142f420a0 and slot 0x88 0x142f44410, both bound by [+0x180] not by the vector; vtable methods 0x142f43500 (remove all), 0x142f45590 and the 0x14f8xxxxx thunk bodies at slots 0x40/0xd8/0xe0 only read the vector. Cost of the clamp: vehicles past 26 skip this function's per-vehicle setup (component 0x146ce8a00 config copy, vehicle controller set, +0x132 bit 2, +0x2580, +0x9f2c.., 0x144632590); which vehicle that is depends on the vector's order, not shown statically, so a guarded session is crash-free but its 27th+ vehicle is not set up by this call (runtime check).

V2134 TT27V item 4. Agree on memory ownership: the vehicle system (vtable 0x1457f8290) vector is {allocator +0x20, begin +0x28, end +0x30, cap +0x38} of raw entity pointers; it is freed only by vtable slot 0xc0 = 0x142f43500 (pointer at 0x1457f8350; session exit: unregisters its message handlers, logs 'Removing all vehicle from vehicle system', end=begin, allocator(+0x20)->slot 0x38 free(begin), zeroes begin/end/cap) and by the destructor slot 0x8 = 0x142fe77f0 (same sequence). No per-element destructor runs and the free uses begin, so holding end at 26 or putting it back cannot leak or double-free; if the exit already ran, end is 0 and the guard's end==clamped test skips the write. Disagree that holding the vector at 26 is safe: the AI system's per-frame update 0x1405ee110 fills its per-vehicle cache ai+0x128 (16-byte {vehicle, component 0x146ce8b40}) only for i < the byte count of this vector, then schedules job 0x14063e370 (lea at 0x1405ee51e) over [ai+8] AI vehicles; the job takes i by lock xadd and loads rbx = [[ai+0x128]+i*16+8] (0x14063e5dd), then mov r10,[rbx+0x18] (0x14063e889). With 27 AI vehicles and the vector held at 26, entry 26 stays null: IG10 20261030-061735 faults there 23 ms after the guard line (rsi=0x1a, rdi=0x1a0, rbx=0, reading 0x18). A session with 27 vehicles cannot be made safe by shortening this vector; only keeping the session at 26 vehicles upstream is.
